seo.title: CSV and Excel import, XLSX export and backups
seo.description: Import CSV, JSON, Excel and SQL files, export tables and results to formats such as XLSX and Parquet, open data files alone, and back up with dump tools.

header.title: Import and export
header.lead: Import files into tables, export tables and results, and open CSV, JSON or Excel without a database.

bands.title: Export tables and results
text: Export tables and views to {exportFormats}, streaming past the grid’s row cap. SQL engines take a filter, a limit and a column list per table, and a SQL export can include the structure. <ui>Export Results</ui> reruns a capped query to write the whole result, and a free plugin adds {exportPluginFormats}.
notes: A SQL export puts DROP TABLE IF EXISTS before each table unless you turn it off.

bands.title: Import files into a table
text: Import {importFormats} files into a new or existing table, with a column mapping you can save for next time. SQL files run as statements, .sql.gz dumps and SQL Server GO scripts included. An import is one transaction unless you turn that off; when a row fails, roll back, keep what was imported, or skip the failed rows and export them.
notes: Linux imports CSV into an existing table, and SQL files. iPhone and iPad add rows through Shortcuts.

bands.title: Data Files
text: Open delimited text, JSON and JSON Lines as tables, with no connection. Filter, replace text, remove duplicate rows and read each column’s statistics, then save in the original format or import into a table. Excel and compressed files open read-only.

bands.title: Backup and restore
text: Backup Dump and Restore Dump run {backupTools} with the connection’s SSH and TLS settings; you install the tool, except for DuckDB. Server-Side Export on {serverSideExport} writes through Oracle Data Pump, a Snowflake stage or Cloud Storage, so the data never passes through your Mac.
notes: Linux writes SQL dumps without external tools.

more.title: Files that are databases
text: SQLite and DuckDB files open from Finder as connections. A SQLite file on an SSH server opens live or as a read-only copy, and DuckDB reads Parquet, CSV and JSON as views.

more.title: From one database to another
text: Copy or transfer tables between connections without a file in between.

more.title: On iPhone and iPad
text: Copy or share rows as JSON, CSV or INSERT statements, and add rows with the Shortcuts actions.
